To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adult bone marrow stem cells can give rise to liver cells, and that only purified hematopoietict stem cells can give such a response.
adult bone marrow cells can be transplanted into a mouse with liver disease, and that these cells differentiate into hepatocytes.
adult bone marrow cells, when transplanted into a tyrosinemia model, can give rise to hepatocytes and restore the biochemical function of the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a new cell population with the ability to generate multiple tissues.
the characterization of the cells that are capable of regenerating the liver in the absence of hepatocytes, and the molecular mechanisms that regulate their differentiation.
the identification of the cellular origin and differentiation pathways of hepatic progenitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hematopoietetic stem cell is the only cell type capable of giving rise to both hematopoietic progenitors and hepatocytes, but that the hematopoetic stem cell is not a progenitor of either cell type.

the hematopoietically derived hepatic cells in the FAI−/− mice were not transdifferentiation products of hematopoietic progenitors, but were rather derived from a multipotent stem cell that had the potential to differentiate into both hematopoietic lineages and hepatic progenitor lineages.
bone marrow cells have a high degree of plasticity and can differentiate into hepatocyte-like cells in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hematopoietetic stem cell is the most potent stem cell for hepatic regeneration.

purified hematopoietict stem cells can transdifferentiate into hepatocytes in the FAH −/− mouse, and that the hematopoietict system contains a population of cells that can transdifferentiate and give rise to hepatocytes.
the hematopoietict stem cells are the most primitive cells in bone marrow that can differentiate to hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver can regenerate from bone marrow-derived cells, and that the cells responsible for this regeneration have the phenotype of hematopoietic progenitors.
bone marrow cells can differentiate into functional hepatocytes, which is of great clinical importance for cell therapy in liver diseases.
bone marrow-derived stem cells can differentiate in vivo into hepatocytes.
